text:
incident-bot: [AUTO] PAGER: P1 — Network/DNS anomaly in Azure westindia affecting Private Link / on-prem connectors. Elevated 5xxs and DNS resolution errors observed for PrivateConnect customers. Runbook: <https://redwood-internal/runbooks/az-private-dns-multipath>. Pager details and affected tenants attached.

Dinesh: oncall here, ack. jumping in. marking paging channel and starting runbook. initial hypothesis: DNS multipath + egress route divergence between two Azure egress clusters causing inconsistent next-hops for private endpoints.

Maria: seeing spikes across three tenants — tenant-a, tenant-b, tenant-c. 502s started ~2026-03-15T09:11:00Z, peak 09:14:00Z. Token throughput roughly stable, but per-request error rate to private-hosted endpoints up ~12%.

Linh: I pulled a few DNS traces from westindia private DNS zone. dig output looks weird — sometimes NXDOMAIN, sometimes two different A records with wildly different TTLs. paste:```
; dig +short private.svc.tenant-a.internal
10.4.5.21
; dig +short private.svc.tenant-a.internal
10.4.5.21
10.8.1.7
; dig +short private.svc.tenant-a.internal
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
This matches BGP adjacency flapping I see on our ExpressRoute-like peering: two next-hops alternating.

Dinesh: running runbook step 2 — isolate impacted vnets and apply egress route policy to prefer regional-egress-2 (fallback). Executed (truncated):```
az network vnet update -n vnet-tenant-a -g prod-vnets --set properties.egressPolicy.preferred=regional-egress-2
# verified route table change: 0 -> regional-egress-2
```
Applying to tenant-b now. Will monitor metrics.

Support-Sarah: pinging support ops: we've opened initial customer comms. Notifying tenant-a and tenant-b with suggested immediate mitigation: restart on-prem connector, enable "prefer-hosted-fallback" flag (if available), or move traffic to public-hosted endpoint for the next 30m. Template sent: "We're investigating routing/DNS instability in Azure West India affecting PrivateLink access. Temporary workaround: switch to hosted endpoints or restart on-prem connector. We'll follow up with timeline." :phone: :email:

Incident-bot: Incident channel created and tagged Incident-2026-03-15-az-westindia. Severity set to P1. Playbook: Networking > DNS multipath.

Sam: taking over oncall at 09:40Z — thanks @dinesh. Observed real-time metrics: after route policy change, 502s for tenant-a dropped from 14% -> 3% within 4 minutes. tenant-b improved partially, tenant-c still noisy. DNS still fluctuating for ~12% of queries.

Alex: quick question — can we enable auto-fallback in the platform for PrivateConnect requests to try public endpoints when DNS fails? If not safe, we can roll a short-lived config flag:```
# toggle fallback for env prod
redwood-config set private_fallback=true --scope tenant-a,tenant-b --ttl 1800
```
Should reduce customer impact while Azure investigates.

Customer-ops: tenant-c just reported the fallback didn't apply — their connector has strict routing. We provided manual switchover steps and a small script to update their route preferences. Sent instructions at 09:52Z.

Dinesh: updated Azure SR: 9876543210 with support engineer. Provided BGP dumps and DNS traces. Azure support acknowledges and is engaging their backbone team. Requesting mitigation ETA.

Maria: summary for execs: Impacted region: Azure westindia. Impact window start: ~2026-03-15T09:11Z. Scope: 3 known tenants on PrivateConnect (tenant-a/b/c), broader telemetry shows <1% of all private connections but concentrated customer-visible errors for those three. Mitigation in flight: route-policy failover + platform fallback flag for some tenants. Next: await Azure SR updates and verify long-term fix (route convergence / DNS consistency).

Support-Sarah: customers updated at 10:02Z. Two customers requested incident bridge — set up a short customer-facing bridge for tenant-c at 10:10Z.

Sam: new observation — when traffic hits regional-egress-2 consistently, latency improves but we still see occasional NXDOMAIN from the private DNS system for some subnets. Suggest we add DNS retry logic in client SDK to try secondary resolver for the next 30 minutes. I'll open a quick PR for a hotfix: increase dns retries to 3 with jitter.

Linh: Azure replied to SR: "We've seen an internal control-plane reconvergence between egress clusters causing transient DNS authoritative divergence. We are applying a staged fix and will monitor propagation. Estimated stabilization 20-45 minutes." copying SR note.

Maria: setting incident state -> MITIGATING. On-call: @sam is incident lead. Please keep channel updated with SR updates and customer bridge minutes.

Dinesh: handing back context to @sam, leaving post-incident follow-up items in the runbook. I'll update the notes and hand off. :white_check_mark:

Incident-bot: Pager cleared at 10:18Z — system-level errors trending down to baseline. Incident remains open while we wait for Azure confirmation and runbook postmortem.

Support-Sarah: last update to customers at 10:25Z: "Azure reports control-plane fix in progress; we see improved success rates for most, and will confirm when all propagation complete. We will follow up with a full incident report."

Sam: final note before I move this to postmortem queue — mitigation reduced customer-visible errors to <1% across affected tenants. We'll keep SR open until Azure confirms full control-plane convergence, then schedule a blameless postmortem with networking and platform teams. Thanks everyone. :pray:
